recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Romie's case for antiquated transhumanism", "body": "Homie Romie opens with a prepared statement arguing that human beings are simple, electrically attuned beings whose connection to the source field gets clouded by the muck in our minds. He describes recorded history as a sine wave slipping in and out of truth, and suggests a major cover-up took place somewhere between the 14th and 19th centuries. In his view the motives of those pulling the strings have not changed since Plato's cave, yet he insists antiquated transhumanism is not all negative: he calls it magic with different shades, and says it is up to each person what they tap into."}, {"title": "Questioning where modern transhumanism leads", "body": "Romie reads Max More's definition of transhumanism and a 2011 ExtremeTech prediction that chip implants, virtual currencies and brainwave reading devices would turn globalization into a full sprint. His objection, he says, is not the relationship between humans and technology but their merging, and he expects products like Neuralink to be sold with feel-good ads while the data mining goes unmentioned. Chance notes that a prosthetic leg technically counts as transhumanism, then asks how much of our technology plagiarizes abilities humans might have naturally, pointing to the flying he does in dreams and calling the word quantum a stand-in for magic."}, {"title": "Romie's view of crowns as consciousness tools", "body": "Romie points out that royal crowns appear in nearly every culture, tracing them back to Egypt, and argues that the textbook framing of crowns as symbols of political power misses their esoteric purpose: resonating with the gods and like a god. Chance describes how intense a quartz and moldavite pendant felt when he first wore it, and shares his understanding that early Egyptian pharaohs were chosen from the most learned priests. Discussing the fortress crowns of Cronos and Rhea, Romie says what first tipped him off was how closely crowns resemble the spires atop cathedrals, likening the body to the earth and the crown to its resonant architecture."}, {"title": "Crowns, crows and the roots of words", "body": "Romie reads being crowned king as crowning, a cosmic birth, and links it to the alchemical crow that marks putrefaction, which he calls the first step of the process. Chance runs the Latin corvus through small phonetic shifts toward Cronus, and Romie's slides lay out etymologists' competing roots for corona. Touring crowns from Albania to Portugal, the pair read Skanderbeg's helmet with its bronze goat head as a nod to the ram horns of Amun Ra, which Chance follows through Zeus Ammon and the horned Moses, before Chance turns the red crown of Lower Egypt into a joke about the masses and asses."}, {"title": "Astrological ages and a watered down history", "body": "Both men read the astrological ages as a frame for what has been lost. Chance treats the great flood as symbolic as well as physical, calling the Piscean deluge a delusion of rival gods and pantheons that hid a shared hero's journey. He suggests the ages run backwards from a high point in Aries, while Romie argues the age of Pisces watered down history, from cheap neo renaissance building to church bells he says once resonated along ley lines. Chance cites Michael Tsarion's idea that knowledge spread from a far northern homeland, and Romie recommends the book Beyond the North Wind on Hyperborea."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Homie Romie of the Rising From The Ashes Podcast blesses us with an original presentation of his antiquated transhumanism thesis. In the first segment we discuss the mechanics of human-to-ether cloud consciousness and the possible tools used to achieve it from the ancient world, taking an extensive look at the royal crowns.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension our exploration expands to dowsing rods and the hidden divining tools & techniques of the alchemical initiates. We also look at other royal devices, such as scepters, swords, the globus cruciger, bells, and other magical talismans.
